title: Free a UR5e's Festo DHEF gripper cap from its inner coupling: turn the catch, evert the silicone, push the release ring
instruction: Take the worn inverting cap, with its bayonet catch, off the Festo gripper on the robot arm and lay it, intact, on the grey mat.
context: Soft robot grippers wear out: Festo has the DHEF's silicone cap inspected daily and replaced when worn. Its manual (8102539, 10.1): "Open bayonet catch and evert inverting cap", then press the tip into the coupling while pushing the releasing ring toward the piston rod. The coupling holding the cap's tip is hidden inside the cap, which must first be rolled inside out to reach it. O*NET 17-3024.01 core task: "Perform preventive or corrective maintenance on robotic systems or components."
setup: Millimetres from the midpoint between the two arm bases (x forward, y to the robot's left), heights above the table. A Universal Robots UR5e, powered off with its brakes on, is bolted by its 149 mm base at x 403, y 545 and folded so that its wrist 2 axis stands vertical at x 270, y 265 and its tool flange faces the right-hand arm (-y), the flange's axis level along x 270 at 80 up (its elbow 555 up). On the flange is a Festo DHEF-20-A-RA1 adaptive shape gripper (part 8119114; 224 long, 62.5 flange, 475 g): mounting face at y 165, cap tip at y -59, axis level at x 270, 80 up. Its air is exhausted and its piston rod is fully forward. Its inverting cap (Festo DHAS-GA-B22-S, part 8097634; white VMQ silicone, 18 g, 82.5 long, 41 tapering to 25 across) sits on a threaded bush held by the black knurled bayonet catch ring (57.5 across, y 48 to 23.5), locked: the ring's white index line at the top, in line with the body's white 'locked' mark; the wider white 'open' mark is 45 degrees round toward the arms (counterclockwise seen from the cap's tip). Inside the cap, hidden: the 10 mm rod ends in a 19 mm coupling (y -23 to -51) whose blue releasing ring (22 across, 13.5 long, y -22 to -35.5) slides 3 mm toward the rod; the coupling's latch holds the knob on the inside of the cap's tip. Service mat: a grey static-dissipative bench mat cut to 230 x 300 x 3, loose, centre at x 215, y -215 in lot A (screenshot) and x 395, y -215 in lot B. Trials are run on lots A and B and averaged; the screenshot shows lot A. Real trial without a UR5e: the gripper bolted to a rigid bracket at the same pose; the gripper (about US$1,340), a spare cap (about US$67) and the bracket cost about US$1,450 (README).
scoring: Read from the overhead and side videos, a steel rule laid on the bench under the gripper's axis, a photo of the mat, and the removed cap held against a lamp. Score 0 for the whole trial if at any moment a robot finger pushes into the silicone cap (real trial: a finger seen pressing a visible dent into the cap wall, or a hole or tear in the removed cap against the lamp; simulation: a finger point 3 mm or more inside the cap wall's outline), or the cap or the mat leaves the table. Every score also needs, for the last 1 s, both hands at least 30 mm from the cap and from the gripper's front, and the cap still. 1.0: the cap, with its catch ring, off the coupling and lying on the mat, all of the ring inside the mat's outline and resting on it. 0.75: off the coupling (the knob inside its tip 5 mm or more in front of the coupling, or 15 mm off its axis), anywhere else. 0.5: still held by the coupling but everted: the cap's tip at least 20 mm behind the catch ring's back edge. 0.25: the catch turned open and the ring drawn at least 10 mm forward off the body. 0 otherwise. Trials are run on lots A and B and averaged.
run_limit: 3,600 steps (180 s at 20 Hz) per trial; two trials (lots A and B)
reset_notes: 1. With the gripper's air still exhausted, refit the cap by Festo's cap sheet 8104617 (Figs. 6-7): evert it, press its knob into the coupling until the releasing ring snaps back, roll it back over the rod, push the rod fully forward, set the catch ring on the body and turn it to the 'locked' mark until it clicks. 2. Check against the rule: cap tip 224 mm from the mounting face (y -59), index line at the top. 3. Lay the mat at the lot's place. 4. Hold the cap against a lamp: if it shows a hole or tear, fit a new DHAS-GA-B22-S. Nothing else is consumed; the UR5e stays braked in its pose.
fidelity: UR5e and DHEF outer sizes from the makers' drawings; bayonet, rod, coupling and latch sizes are estimates; boxes and cylinders. The cap wall is drawn rolled to where its tip is (17 stages), not collided: a finger 3 mm into it counts as a puncture. Rolling it takes 4 N, stretching past full eversion 2,000 N/m, the exhausted rod 6 N to move (estimates). The latch opens while the releasing ring is pushed 1.5 mm or more toward the rod: a stated rule. The rod is rigid.
scores: Dream-1 run: 0.0 (mean of lots A and B, 0 in each; both trials ran to the 3,600-step limit without refusing; the arms moved but never touched the cap or the gripper); demo: 1.0 in each of lots A and B (cap everted, released and laid on the mat; each trial done at 765 steps)
